name: oddbout
description: Create, review and register your ODDBOUT fighter from a PC or a supported Dots workspace.

interface.shortDescription: Create, review and register your fighter
interface.longDescription: Create your ODDBOUT fighter from an idea or reference image. Review appearance and animation groups, preserve chosen versions, resume unfinished work and register the approved package with your connected ODDBOUT account. Creation runs in your PC or a supported per-user Dots workspace with Node.js 22.12+, Python 3.11+ and your own generation account. Registration uses the same Google-connected ODDBOUT tools in either environment. A chat without execution or file delivery cannot complete animation packaging. Generation access, usage charges and visual approval remain separate.
defaultPrompt: Help me create and register my ODDBOUT fighter.
Resume my fighter and show what still needs review.

publication.release_notes: 0.5.3: Packing and gait checks run faster; an approved device sign-in survives a network failure and finishes with --device-wait; recording a version after an interrupted copy works; saving the session retries a briefly locked file on Windows; updates that change the validator or tools ask for a restart. 0.5.2: A session lock left by an interrupted run is reclaimed instead of blocking the session; parallel tool calls wait their turn; a finished generation is always recorded; game-context failures say whether the kit needs an update; profile text limits match the package contract. 0.5.1: fighter:pack and fighter:gait run again (0.5.0 left out a module they import), and a package that fails file validation is no longer written to its folder. 0.5.0: The sprite-gen engine is now sprite-gen-agent (Alex Kim's sprite-gen 3.4.0 with the motion engine); no hash patch step. 0.4.0: One ODDBOUT entry point for creation, grouped review and registration. Run the same workspace tools from a PC or a supported Dots workspace without a separate local MCP plugin. Use the existing connected ODDBOUT account for registration; preserve local projects and selected versions.
